content:
Apple's highly anticipated AI smart glasses are finally getting a release date, expected to launch at the end of next year.

WWDC27 Reveal

Earlier this year, reports suggested that Apple's AI smart glasses would officially go on sale in late 2027. Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman's report today maintains that claim. However, we now know that Apple is currently "pushing" to unveil the new glasses to the public at next year's Worldwide Developers Conference.

The timing of this announcement may hint at the future direction of Apple's AI glasses. Without simultaneously rolling out a way for developers to write software for the device, Apple seems unlikely to announce new hardware at WWDC. Therefore, the glasses may be able to integrate third-party app data and operations like the new AI Siri, rather than being limited to Apple's own features.

If all goes well, this would be very similar to the 2023 launch of the Apple Vision Pro: hardware and software previewed months in advance, allowing developers to build apps for the platform, with the hardware eventually shipping later.

Privacy Concerns

One reason Apple's glasses have been delayed from their original late 2026 launch is the company's ongoing efforts to address privacy issues. Similar products from companies like Meta have faced criticism, opposition, and even bans in some venues due to privacy concerns over the cameras. According to Gurman, Apple is exploring multiple solutions. In addition to testing a version with no cameras at all, Apple is also considering software-based solutions:

Beyond these measures, Apple is reportedly also "developing a range of new hardware- and software-related privacy features not found in any existing products."

Wrap-Up

Apple's AI glasses won't have any display, but are expected to take photos, play music, converse with Siri, and take calls. They're also expected to feature a unique, stylish design that sets them apart from competitors. Are you interested in this product? Let us know in the comments!
